technical-data.invention-title: ILLUMINATION LAMP HAVING BRIGHTNESS AND COLOR CONTROL
LAMPE D'ECLAIRAGE A REGULATION DE LA LUMINOSITE ET DE LA COULEUR

abstract.p: An illumination lamp allows a user to perform brightness and color control in accordance with the state and purpose of use, the environment of use or the tastes of the users. The illumination lamp may include a rectifier (1) for rectifying a current supplied by a power supply; a ballast portion (2) for starting the lamp using the power rectified in the rectifier; a lamp portion (3) that is connected to the ballast portion (2) and that includes more than two tubes (13), each tube (13) having a different color temperature; and a controller (4) that is connected to the ballast portion (2), for controlling a brightness and color of light produced by the illumination lamp.

Lampe d'éclairage qui permet à un utilisateur de réguler la luminosité et la couleur selon la situation et le but d'utilisation, l'environnement ou le goût de l'utilisateur. Ladite lampe peut comporter un redresseur (1) destiné à redresser un courant fourni par une alimentation électrique, une partie ballast (2) destinée à l'allumage de la lampe à l'aide du courant redressé dans le redresseur, une partie lampe (3), connectée à la partie ballast (2), qui comporte deux tubes (13) ou plus, chaque tube ayant une température de couleur différente, et un dispositif de commande (4) connecté à la partie ballast (2) et destiné à réguler la luminosité et la couleur produites par ladite lampe d'éclairage.

description.p: ILLUMINATION LAMP HAVING BRIGHTNESS AND COLOR CONTROL
Technical Field
The present invention relates to an illumination lamp
which allows a user to perform a variety of brightness and
color controls in accordance with the tastes of the users,
or a state of use.
Background Art
A conventional illumination lamp generally has a
single color, with a specified brightness.
Recently, there is a growing tendency to use three
lamps that output different wavelengths of light to provide
a more natural light projection. However, it is impossible
to control the brightness or red (R) , green (G) , and blue
(B) colors of the recently developed three-wavelength lamps
in accordance with the place of use or tastes of users.
Although every person has different taste, the optimal
brightness of a lamp is approximately 4000K in the morning,
6000K in the afternoon, and 3000K in the evening.
Unfortunately, the brightness and color of conventional

illumination lamps are not controlled automatically or
manually .
Disclosure of Invention
Accordingly, the present invention is directed to an
illumination lamp having brightness and color controls that
substantially obviates one or more of the limitations and
disadvantages of the related art.
An object of the present invention is to provide an
illumination lamp for performing optional brightness and
color control according to the state and purpose of use or
the environment of use and the tastes of users.
Additional features and advantages of the invention
will be set forth in part in the description which follows
and in part will become apparent to those having ordinary
skill in the art upon examination of the following or may
be learned from practice of the invention. The objects and
advantages of the invention may be realized and attained as
particularly pointed out in the appended claims.
To achieve these and other advantages, and in
accordance with the purpose of the present invention as
embodied and broadly described, the illumination lamp

includes: a rectifier for rectifying a current supplied by
a power supply; a ballast portion for lighting up the
illumination lamp using the power rectified in the
rectifier; a lamp that is connected to the ballast portion
and that consists of more than two light generating
devices, each light generating device having a different
color temperature; and a controller that is connected to
the ballast portion, for controlling a brightness and color
of light output by the lamp.
The controller may be connected to a display unit
comprising a display panel of light emitting diodes (LEDs),
or to a control stick. The controller is used to control
the brightness and/or color temperature of the device in
accordance with an operating state, the operating
environment, or the tastes of the user.
It is to be understood that both the foregoing general
description and the following detailed description are
exemplary and explanatory and are intended to provide
further explanation of the invention as claimed.
Brief Description of Drawings
The accompanying drawings, which are included to

provide a further understanding of the invention and are
incorporated in and constitute a part of this
specification, illustrate embodiments of the invention and
together with the description serve to explain the
principles of the invention.
Figure 1 is a schematic block diagram of an
illumination lamp according to the present invention;
Figure 2 is a partial block diagram of another
embodiment according to the present invention;
Figure 3 is a schematic diagram of the display unit
depicted in Figure 2; and
Figure 4 is a partial block diagram of another
embodiment of according to the present invention.
Best Mode for carrying Out the Invention
Reference will now be made in detail to the preferred
embodiments of the present invention, examples of which are
illustrated in the accompanying drawings.
Figure 1 schematically shows a structure of an
illumination lamp in accordance with the present invention.
The illumination lamp includes a rectifier 1 for performing
power supply rectification, a ballast portion 2, and a lamp

3 for providing illumination. In this embodiment of the
invention, the lamp 3 is composed of more than two gas
discharge tubes 13, each representing a different color
temperature. In a preferred embodiment, the lamp 3 consists
of red (R) , green (G) and blue (B) gas discharge tubes.
As shown in the drawing, ballasts 12 connected to the
respective tubes 13, are also connected to a controller 4
for controlling the ballasts 12. As a result, all the
ballasts 12 can be controlled separate from one another,
and they are operated automatically within a predetermined
scope, or manually. For instance, in case of general desk
lamp embodying the present invention, in addition to the
basic on/off operation, the controller 4 is operated to
control the color and/or brightness of the lamp, depending
on the environment of study, i.e. the ambient brightness,
the structure of a room, the amount of sunlight, etc.
Figure 2 shows another embodiment of the present
invention where a display unit 21, for indicating the
brightness and color temperature settings, is connected to
the controller 4. The display unit 21 helps a user to
freely control the brightness and color temperature when
necessary.

A display unit 21 which can be incorporated in a
device embodying the invention is shown in Figure 3. The
display comprises a plurality of light emitting diodes
(LEDs) arranged m a diamond shaped pattern. The LEDs are
selectively illuminated to indicate the brightness and
color settings.
As shown m Figure 3, the x-axis of the display
indicates the color temperature, and the y-axis of the
display indicates the brightness. The control of color
temperature and brightness is established based upon
predetermined values of the color temperature and
brightness on the x and y axes. The display unit 21 allows
a user to select a certain state and to recognize degrees
of color temperature and brightness corresponding to the
selected state through the illumination of the LEDs in the
display 21.
The user can control the brightness and color
temperature of a lamp, depending on the circumstances, by
operating brightness control switches 22a and color
temperature control switches 22b, which may be provided on
sides of the display. The user can adjust the brightness
and color temperature to desired values based upon the

predetermined values.
The display unit 21 may be located in the illumination
lamp. The control switches 22a and 22b can be embodied in
different forms according to a variety of known types, such
as slide type and button type.
In an alternate embodiment of the present invention,
instead of using control switches and a display, as shown
in Figure 3, a control stick 21 (e.g. in the form of a joy
stick), may be connected to the controller 4, as shown in
Figure 4. The control stick 31 would be used to properly
control the color temperature and brightness through
positioning of the control stick 31. The physical location
of the control stick 31 would give an indication of the
brightness and color settings.
A lamp of the present invention provides optimum
illumination by controlling, in a wide range, the light
color and intensity, according to the purpose for which the
lamp is used. For instance, different colors and intensity
values could be used for a desk lamp, an illumination
apparatus, a display lamp, etc.
To obtain different color representation, red, green
and blue color lamps for the basic three-wavelength display

are used together. Two tubes each having a different shape
or outputting different colored light may be associated
with each other, or the tubes are associated with one
another having more subdivided colors .
As described above, illumination lamps of the present
invention may include more than two gas discharge tubes,
each having a different color temperature. The different
tubes are associated with one another, and are controlled
automatically or manually, so that a variety of color and
brightness controls is achieved in accordance with the
purpose or environment of use.
It will be apparent to those skilled in the art that
various modifications and variations can be made in the
illumination lamp having brightness and color control of
the present invention without deviating from the spirit or
scope of the invention. Thus, it is intended that the
present invention cover the modifications and variations of
this invention provided they come within the scope of the
appended claims and their equivalents.
For instance, although the embodiments described above
utilize gas discharge tubes to produce different colors of
light, any type of light generating device could be used.

For instance, the gas discharge tubes could be replaced
with incandescent light bulbs. In this instance, color
filters could be used to obtain different output colors.
Also, an embodiment might use fluorescent or electro¬
luminescent lighting device, or devices that utilize
microwaves to excite a gas in a tube. Any lighting devices
that are capable of outputting colored light could be used.
In the claims, means-plus-function clauses are
intended to cover the structures described herein as
performing the recited function and not only structural
equivalents but also equivalent structures. For example,
although a gas discharge tube and an incandescent light
bulb may not be structural equivalents in that a gas
discharge tube excites a gas to produce light, whereas an
incandescent light bulb employs a heated filament, in the
environment of providing light, a gas discharge tube and an
incandescent light bulb may be equivalent structures.

claim.claim-text: WHAT IS CLAIMED IS:
1. An illumination lamp comprising:
a rectifier for rectifying a current supplied by a
power supply;
a ballast portion for starting the illumination lamp
using the power rectified in the rectifier;
a lamp portion that is connected to the ballast
portion and that comprises more than two light generating
tubes, each light generating tube having a different color
temperature; and
a controller that is connected to the ballast portion,
wherein the controller is configured to control a
brightness and color of light generated by the illumination
lamp.
2. The illumination lamp of claim 1, wherein said
controller comprises:
a display unit with a color temperature control axis
and a brightness control axis that are substantially
perpendicular to each other, wherein the display unit
indicates the orightness and color temperature settings of

the lamp; and
at least ne control switch for controlling a
brightness and color temperature of light generated by the
illumination lεmp.
3. The illumination lamp of claim 2, wherein the at
least one control switch includes a first switch for
controlling a brightness of light generated by the
illumination -, amp and a second switch for controlling a
color temperature of light generated by the illumination
lamp.
4. The l Llummation lamp of claim 2, wherein the
display unit includes a plurality of light emitting diodes
that are selectively illuminated to indicate the brightness
and color temperature settings of the lamp.
5. The illumination lamp of claim 1, wherein said
controller is connected to a control stick that is movable
in at least two substantially perpendicular direction, and
wherein the control stick is configured to control a
brightness and color temperature of light generated by the
illumination Lamp.
6. The illumination lamp of claim 5, wherein a
position of the control stick indicates the brightness and
color temperature settings of the illumination lamp.
7. An illumination lamp, comprising:
a plurality of illumination devices, wherein each
illumination device is configured to produce light having a
different color temperature; and
a controller that is configured to allow a user to
control a brightness and a color temperature of light
generated by the illumination lamp, and wherein the
controller is also configured to indicate the brightness
and color temperature settings of the illumination lamp.
8. The illumination lamp of claim 1 , wherein the
controller comprises a display device that indicates the
brightness and color temperature settings of the
illumination lamp.
9. The illumination lamp of claim 8, wherein the
display device includes a plurality of light emitting
diodes arranged in a two dimensional pattern on the display
device .
10. The illumination lamp of claim 9, wherein the
illumination status of the plurality of light emitting
diodes indicates the brightness and color temperature
settings of the illumination lamp.

11. The illumination lamp of claim 9, wherein the two
dimensional pattern has a first axis that is indicative of
the brightness setting of the illumination lamp and a
second axis that is indicative of the color temperature
setting of the illumination lamp.
12. The illumination lamp of claim 7, wherein the
controller comprises a joystick that is movable in first
and second substantially perpendicular directions, wherein
movement of the joystick in the first direction controls
the brightness setting of the illumination lamp and wherein
movement of the joystick in the second direction controls
the color temperature setting of the illumination lamp.
13. The illumination lamp of claim 12, wherein the
position of the joystick is indicative of both the
brightness and color temperature settings of the
illumination lamp.
14. The illumination lamp of claim 7, wherein the
plurality of illumination devices comprise a plurality of
gas discharge tubes, and wherein each of the gas discharge
tubes is configured to output light having different
wavelength characteristics.
15. The illumination lamp of claim 14, further

comprising a ballast unit for controlling each of the
plurality of gas discharge tubes, wherein the controller is
connected to and controls the ballast unit.
16. An illumination lamp, comprising:
means for producing light, wherein the light producing
means is configured so that a brightness and a color
temperature of the light may be selectively varied;
means for controlling the brightness and the color
temperature of light generated by the light producing means
based on a user input; and
means for displaying the brightness and temperature
settings .
17. The illumination lamp of claim 16, wherein the
light producing means comprises a plurality of means for
producing light, and wherein each of the plurality of light
producing means is configured to generate light having a
different color temperature.
18. The illumination lamp of claim 16, wherein the
controlling means comprises:
means for controlling the brightness of the light
generated by the light producing means; and
means for controlling the color temperature of the
light generated by the light producing means.
19. The illumination lamp of claim 16, wherein the
controlling means includes a control lever, and wherein the
position of the control lever indicates brightness and
color temperature settings.
20. The illumination lamp of claim 16, wherein the
displaying means includes a two dimensional display, and
wherein a position of a market on the two dimensional
display indicates both a brightness and a color temperature
setting of the illumination lamp.
